learning_outcomes.text: Explains the basic structure and components of composite materials.
Analyzes the functions of matrix and reinforcement elements.
Compares different fiber types (glass, carbon, aramid).
Distinguishes between thermoset and thermoplastic polymer matrix systems.
Interprets fiber-matrix interaction and interface behavior.
Evaluates the mechanical behaviors of composite materials.
Selects appropriate composite materials for engineering applications.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to composite materials and basic concepts
Advantages and application areas of composite materials
Definition and functions of matrix and reinforcement elements
Glass fibers: production, properties, and application areas
Carbon fibers: production, properties, and application areas
Aramid fibers and other fiber types
Production methods: hand lay-up, vacuum infusion, prepreg
Mechanical behavior and damage mechanisms of composite materials
assessment_rules: Midterm and final exam dates are not specified in the 14-week course plan; they are held on dates specified in the academic calendar by the decision of the University Senate.
